answer: A lantern carried at dawn lights one street at a time; a thousand accounts cannot all be holding it. So make verification a matter of presence: the ledger issues a task that expires within minutes, forcing not raw compute but continuous human-scale attention. To farm sybils then, an operator must keep many masks simultaneously awake and alert - a cost paid in sleepless hours, not coins. An onyx still in the mine answers no one; only a present identity can.
